MG01.analysis: Goal: open stuck lid with no edge to pry. Standard: pry with a lever; blocked since the edge is flush. Real bottleneck is lack of grip, not lack of a gap. Rubber band and sock add friction; a spoon handle can tap the seam to break the seal. Better than prying, and feasible.
MG01.final:
step1: Stretch the rubber band around the lid (or over its top surface) to create a high-friction grip.
step2: Wear the thin socks on your hands for extra friction and twist/pull the lid, tapping around the seam with the wooden spoon handle to break the seal.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG02.analysis: Goal: a planting hole in rocky soil without a spade. Standard: dig. Bottleneck: no digging tool and hard ground. The hose can act as the excavator: high-pressure water erodes soil and exposes roots. Bucket and spoon remove the slurry.
MG02.final:
step1: Use the high-pressure hose to blast and loosen the soil and small rocks at the planting spot, making a hole (hydro-excavation).
step2: Scoop out the slurry and loose stones with the bucket and soup spoon.
step3: Set the tree in the hole, backfill with the loosened soil using the bucket, and water to settle it.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG03.analysis: Goal: waterproof roof before rain. Standard: lay tarp and fasten down. Bottleneck: holes, curved beam, weak rope. Fold the tarp into several layers so holes do not line up; the curved beam, arched upward, acts as a ridge that sheds water; screws, not rope, do the fastening.
MG03.final:
step1: Fold the tarp into 2-3 layers, offsetting the holes so the layers cover each other.
step2: Place the curved beam across the coop top, arch up, as a ridge and screw it to the walls.
step3: Drape the folded tarp over the beam (use the pitchfork to push it up) and screw its edges to the walls; use the rope only as extra ties.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG04.analysis: Goal: remove lice and nits. Standard: medicated shampoo. Unavailable. Vinegar is ruled out by allergy; curler and dryer are useless. Remaining function: oil smothers/loosens lice, fine comb physically removes them, shower cap keeps oil on. Wet-combing works without chemicals.
MG04.final:
step1: Rub the small amount of olive oil through the hair, working it in sparingly to coat the strands.
step2: Cover with the shower cap (handle gently) for an hour or more to smother lice.
step3: Remove the cap and comb section by section with the fine-tooth comb, wiping it clean after each pass; repeat every few days for 2 weeks.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG05.analysis: Goal: working clock power. Standard: swap in a fresh battery. Missing a correct one; contacts are corroded. Function needed: clean contacts (vinegar acid neutralizes alkaline corrosion) and bridge the size gap with conductive foil spacer, so the spare cell can contact both terminals.
MG05.final:
step1: Dip a cotton swab in vinegar, scrub the corrosion off the battery contacts, and dry them.
step2: Fold the aluminum foil into a small pad and place it against a contact as a spacer, so the smaller spare button battery touches both terminals.
step3: Hold the arrangement in place with a bit of thread or card and check that the clock runs (the cell must be about 1.5 V).
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG06.analysis: Goal: paint the high part of a 15 ft wall safely. Standard: ladder. Bottleneck: no ladder and weak bamboo cannot support weight. Weak bamboo only has to carry a brush, not a person. Lash lengths into a long pole, stay on the ground. Tarp protects the ground.
MG06.final:
step1: Lay the tarp at the wall base to catch drips.
step2: Lash several bamboo lengths end-to-end/overlapping with the cotton rope to form a long extension pole, and tie the brush or roller to the tip.
step3: Standing safely on the ground (optionally on one tire for a few extra inches), paint the high section with the pole, working top down.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG07.analysis: Goal: coefficient of friction without force sensor. Standard: pull block with sensor. Alternative: inclined plane; at the angle where a block just slips, mu = tan(theta). Needs only protractor, a ramp surface, a mass; no force reading and no fine ruler needed.
MG07.final:
step1: Use the ruler as a ramp (or a board), pivoting on the nail/pencil; attach the sandpaper to the ramp if it is one of the surfaces tested.
step2: Place a weight on it and slowly raise one end until the weight just starts sliding.
step3: Measure the angle with the protractor; mu = tan(angle). Repeat a few times and average.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG08.analysis: Goal: reach the ground from a 10-story roof. Standard: use the stairwell. Door jammed; lever tools are weak (termite plank, wooden handle) on a steel door. 15 ft rope covers only about 1.5 stories, and the kite cannot carry a person. Descending by self is not feasible; only signaling for rescue is.
MG08.final:
Not possible to get yourself down: the steel door cannot realistically be forced with a broom handle or a termite-eaten plank, and a 15-foot rope is far too short for a ten-story drop (the kite cannot carry a person). The only safe option is to signal for rescue (torch, banging the bucket, waving the kite) and wait.
VERDICT: UNSOLVABLE

MG09.analysis: Goal: sun shade at the beach. Standard: umbrella. Broken. Poncho leaks light through tears, sticks are short. Function: layered fabric for opacity, anchors in sand for height. Towel covers the tears; fins are extra long supports.
MG09.final:
step1: Push the two sticks (and optionally upright fins) into the sand as short posts.
step2: Lay the poncho over them, then layer the large towel on top so it covers the tears, forming a low lean-to.
step3: Weigh the edges down with sand (fill the mug as a weight) and sit in the shade.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG10.analysis: Goal: make the bell ring. Standard: climb or reach with a pole. Climbing banned, rope too short, stool useless for height. Bell rings if struck, so reach is not needed: a thrown object can deliver the strike. Rock is dense and throwable.
MG10.final:
step1: Stand under the pole and throw the rock upward at the bell (about 20 ft is within a normal overarm/underarm throw).
step2: If you miss, retrieve it and repeat; the bottle can be thrown as a backup.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE
